title: Causes of hyperkalemia
text: Common causes of a high serum potassium are reduced kidney excretion (acute kidney injury or chronic kidney disease), drugs that block the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists such as spironolactone), potassium supplements or salt substitutes, and tissue breakdown. A hemolyzed sample can falsely raise the value.

title: When hyperkalemia needs emergency care
text: A potassium of 6.0 mmol/L or higher, any ECG change, muscle weakness, or an irregular or slow pulse warrants same-day emergency evaluation with cardiac monitoring. Outpatient management is reserved for mild elevations without symptoms or ECG changes.

title: Defining acute kidney injury
text: Acute kidney injury is a rise in serum creatinine of at least 0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours, a rise to at least 1.5 times the baseline within 7 days, or reduced urine output. Compare with a prior creatinine to tell acute injury from stable chronic disease.

title: Managing drug-induced hyperkalemia
text: When hyperkalemia follows a new mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist or other renin-angiotensin-aldosterone blocker, stop or hold the drug, avoid potassium supplements, and recheck potassium and creatinine after the acute episode.

title: Hypothyroidism and fatigue
text: Hypothyroidism causes fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain, and constipation. A normal thyrotropin (TSH) makes primary hypothyroidism unlikely.

title: Low potassium
text: Hypokalemia also causes weakness and palpitations, typically after diuretics, vomiting, or diarrhea. Potassium chloride replacement is used only when the measured potassium is low.

title: Fatigue and dyspnea in heart failure
text: Heart failure presents with exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, leg swelling, and jugular venous distension. Its absence on history and exam lowers the likelihood.

title: First tests for fatigue
text: An initial workup for unexplained fatigue usually includes a blood count, a basic metabolic panel with potassium and creatinine, glucose, and thyrotropin.
